Get coordinates of nodes in a gGraph or gData object

Source: R/accessors.R
getCoords.Rd

The function getCoords returns the coordinates (longitude and latitude) of nodes in a gGraph or gData object.

Usage

getCoords(x, ...)

# S4 method for class 'gGraph'
getCoords(x, ...)

# S4 method for class 'gData'
getCoords(x, original = TRUE, ...)

Arguments

x

a valid gGraph or gData object.

...

additional arguments passed to other methods (currently unused).

original

logical. If TRUE (default), returns the original location coordinates; if FALSE, returns the coordinates of the matched nodes on the gGraph grid.

Value

A matrix with two columns, lon and lat, giving the longitude and latitude of each node or location.

Functions

  • getCoords(gGraph): Method for gGraph objects

  • getCoords(gData): Method for gData objects

See also

getNodes, getGraph

Other accessor_methods: getColors(), getCosts(), getData(), getEdges(), getGraph(), getNodes(), getNodesAttr()

Examples

head(getCoords(worldgraph.10k))
#>          lon       lat
#> 1 -179.99999  90.00000
#> 2  144.00002 -90.00000
#> 3  -33.78060  27.18924
#> 4  -32.44279  25.47768
#> 5  -31.14781  23.76450
#> 6  -29.89332  22.05309
